title: myCHEF vs CateringServiceDubai: which is better in 2026
body_markdown:
Choose **myCHEF** if you want a vetted chef or a fully designed event, with the menu built around your guest count, kitchen and dietary needs. Choose **CateringServiceDubai** if a quote from them matches your date and brief on price and format, and they confirm the points in the checklist below in writing. This page compares the two on how you should decide, not on claims we cannot verify.


**TL;DR**

- myCHEF vs CateringServiceDubai in 2026 comes down to service model: vetted chef and designed menu versus a catering quote you must verify.
- myCHEF suits households, dinner parties, weekly meal prep, corporate events and large celebrations in Dubai.
- Ask CateringServiceDubai for written answers on staffing, halal handling, cleanup and what the quote excludes.
- Compare two proposals line by line before paying a deposit with either provider.


## Why this comparison matters in 2026

Dubai has dozens of caterers and private chef services, and their proposals rarely look alike. One quote lists food only. Another bundles staff, equipment and cleanup. Comparing totals without comparing inclusions is the most common way hosts overpay or under-plan.

This page gives you a fair frame for the **myCHEF vs CateringServiceDubai** decision. Everything stated about myCHEF comes from how the service works. For CateringServiceDubai, the table tells you what to ask, because their terms are theirs to confirm. If you are still building a shortlist, the [guide to catering companies in Dubai](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/best-catering-companies-in-dubai) covers the wider field.

## At a glance

| Dimension | myCHEF | CateringServiceDubai |
|---|---|---|
| Best for | Households and hosts who want a vetted chef and a menu designed around them | Hosts who already have a brief and want to compare a straightforward catering quote |
| Service model | Private chef visits and catered events, from home-cooked meals to large celebrations | Ask for the exact formats offered: drop-off, full service or on-site chef |
| Chef selection | Chefs are vetted and scored before they cook for you | Ask who cooks, and how they are selected |
| Menu design | Built around guest count, dietary needs and occasion | Ask whether the menu is fixed, adapted or fully custom |
| Halal handling | Halal-first standards | Ask for written confirmation of sourcing and preparation |
| Cleanup | Kitchen left exactly as we found it | Ask whether cleanup is included or charged separately |
| Pricing model | Starting prices, then a tailored quote for your date and guest count | Ask for an itemised quote with exclusions listed |
| Standout feature | Recurring and one-off service from one provider | Confirm what they consider their specialty |

## myCHEF is built around the client, not the package

The core difference is the starting point. myCHEF begins with your household or event: who is eating, what they eat, what your kitchen can handle and when. The menu follows from that brief, not from a fixed set menu you adjust afterwards.

That suits you if your needs are specific. Think of a family that wants home-cooked meals through the week, a host planning a dinner party with mixed dietary requirements, or a company organising a corporate event with a defined guest count.

The trade-off is real. A designed service involves a short brief before you get a number. If you want to compare ten prices in ten minutes, a catalogue-style caterer may feel faster.

## Chef vetting: myCHEF has a documented standard

**myCHEF is the stronger choice when who cooks matters.** Chefs are vetted and scored before they work with clients. In a private home, that process is the product: you are letting someone into your kitchen.

For CateringServiceDubai, ask three things before you book:

- Who will cook at your event, and will it be the same person each time?
- How are cooks selected and assessed?
- Can you see the proposed menu from the person who will prepare it?

If a provider cannot answer those clearly, treat that as information. Our guide on [whether it is safe to let a private chef cook in your home](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/is-it-safe-to-let-a-private-chef-cook-in-my-home-in-dubai) lists what a good vetting process looks like.

## Menu design is a tie until you see the proposal

Both providers can in principle offer a good menu. The difference shows in how the menu is reached.

With myCHEF, menu design is part of the service: guest counts, dietary needs and the occasion shape the proposal. With any caterer, the useful test is the same. Send an identical brief to both and compare how specific the replies are.

A strong proposal names dishes, portions per guest and what is prepared on site versus delivered. A weak one lists categories such as "starters, mains, desserts" with no detail.

## Halal standards: ask for it in writing

**myCHEF works to halal-first standards.** In the UAE that is the baseline expectation for most hosts, but the detail varies between providers. Sourcing, preparation surfaces and alcohol-adjacent ingredients in sauces are where gaps appear.

Whichever provider you choose, request a written statement covering sourcing and preparation. You can also read how the field compares in our [halal catering roundup](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/best-halal-catering-companies-in-dubai).

## Staffing and cleanup: a question of inclusions

This is where two quotes with similar totals can describe very different services. A chef who cooks and leaves is not the same as a team that cooks, serves and resets the space.

myCHEF's standard is that your kitchen is left exactly as we found it. For any caterer, ask whether serving staff, equipment, glassware and cleanup are inside the quote or added later. Our explainer on [whether Dubai caterers provide serving staff and cleanup](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/can-catering-companies-in-dubai-provide-serving-staff-and-cleanup) shows how to read those lines.

Both providers deserve the same scrutiny here. Neither wins this dimension until you hold the written inclusions.

## Range of occasions: myCHEF covers recurring and one-off

myCHEF handles home-cooked meals, weekly meal prep, dinner parties, corporate events and large catered celebrations. That range matters if your need changes. A household that starts with weekly meals often adds a dinner party later, and staying with one provider keeps your preferences on file.

If you only need a single drop-off for one office lunch, that range is less relevant. A specialist caterer may be perfectly adequate. Confirm CateringServiceDubai's formats before assuming either way.

## Pricing: compare models, not headline totals

myCHEF quotes from starting prices, then tailors the figure to your date, location and guest count. That makes the total predictable once the brief is agreed, but it means you cannot know the final number from a rate card alone.

A fixed per-head catalogue price is easier to compare at a glance. The cost is that extras tend to arrive afterwards. Neither model is wrong. Whichever you choose, get the quote itemised and check these lines:

- Food and ingredients
- Chef or service staff
- Equipment and tableware
- Delivery or travel
- Cleanup
- Anything listed as an exclusion

For current weekly meal prep numbers, see our guide to [weekly meal prep costs in Dubai](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/how-much-does-weekly-meal-prep-cost-in-dubai-in).

|---|---|
| Chef vetting | myCHEF, on its documented standard |

| Staffing and cleanup | Tie until inclusions are written down |
| Range of occasions | myCHEF, for recurring plus one-off |
| Pricing transparency | Tie; depends on how itemised each quote is |

## Final verdict

**Choose myCHEF if** you want a vetted chef in your home, a menu designed around your household or guest list, and cleanup handled. It fits families, hosts of dinner parties and companies planning events with specific dietary needs.

**Choose CateringServiceDubai if** you have a clear brief, their quote is itemised and matches it, and they confirm staffing, halal handling and cleanup in writing. A comparison is only fair once both proposals are in front of you.

If you want a second comparison against a similar provider, see [myCHEF vs CateringInDubai](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/mychef-vs-cateringindubai-which-is-better-in).

## FAQ


**Is myCHEF better than CateringServiceDubai?**

It depends on the job. myCHEF is the better fit for a vetted chef and a menu designed around your household or event. CateringServiceDubai may suit a simple brief if its written quote confirms the inclusions you need.

**Does myCHEF follow halal standards?**

Yes. myCHEF works to halal-first standards. Tell us about any additional dietary requirements in your brief so the menu is designed around them.

**What should I ask CateringServiceDubai before booking?**

Ask who will cook, whether staff and cleanup are included, how halal sourcing is handled and what the quote excludes. Get every answer in writing before paying a deposit.

**How does myCHEF pricing work?**

myCHEF publishes starting prices and then tailors the quote to your date, location and guest count. Send your brief to receive a figure for your specific event.

**Does a myCHEF chef clean up after cooking?**

Yes. The standard is that your kitchen is left exactly as we found it. Confirm any event-specific cleanup requirements when you request your quote.

**Can I use myCHEF for both regular meals and a one-off party?**

Yes. myCHEF covers home-cooked meals, weekly meal prep, dinner parties, corporate events and large celebrations, so one provider can handle both.


## One last thing

Send the same written brief to both providers and compare how specific each reply is. The provider that asks you good questions about guest count, dietary needs and kitchen access before quoting is usually the one that has planned the event properly.

To start with myCHEF, send your date, location, guest count and the service you need through the [contact page](https://www.mychef.ae/contact) and we will reply with a tailored proposal for 2026.
